title: Training Dynamics Impact Post-Training Quantization Robustness
claim: Once the learning rate decays, the loss keeps improving while quantization error rises sharply, so the two diverge.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared x-axis, dotted learning-rate overlay on twin axis
description: Two line plots sit side by side, and both use training tokens (up to about 1e13) on the x-axis. Panel (a) plots 4-bit quantization error. The curve is olive green and hovers around 0.9–1.0e-2 for most of training. When the learning rate starts to decay, the curve turns orange and shoots up to about 1.8e-2. Panel (b) plots validation loss. The solid olive curve declines steadily and then flattens. A dashed olive curve shows the PTQ (post-training quantized) model and sits slightly above it. In the decay phase both curves turn orange, and the loss drops sharply. A gray dotted line on a secondary right axis shows the learning rate. It stays constant at 2e-4 and then falls. The eye goes first to the orange spike in panel (a). Panel (b) shows loss improving over the same interval, which sets up the divergence.
caption: Evolution of quantization error and validation loss during training of SmolLM3 (Bakouch et al., 2025). We report quantization error and validation loss throughout training under both the constant (η = 2e−4, up to 10T tokens) and annealing phases of the learning rate schedule (whose evolution is shown as dotted lines). As the learning rate decays, validation loss consistently decreases, whereas quantization error rises sharply and to a much greater extent than at any earlier point in training.
abstract: While post-training quantization is widely adopted for efficient deployment of large language models, the mechanisms underlying quantization robustness remain unclear. We conduct a comprehensive analysis of quantization degradation across open-source language model training trajectories up to 32B parameters and 15T training tokens to accurately assess the relationship between training dynamics and quantization performance. Our key finding is that quantization errors in large-scale training runs are driven by a complex interplay between learning rate and other training hyperparameters. Specifically, once learning rates decay, validation loss and quantization error diverge, largely independent of training data scale. To investigate interventions on the training dynamics and identify specific configurations that can modulate quantization robustness favorably, we train our own models in controlled experiments up to 100B tokens. Our results challenge the assumption that increasing dataset scale inherently compromises quantization effectiveness, demonstrating instead that strategic training hyperparameter interventions can improve quantization quality at scale.
